                Settings

                Detected from the exports. Change it if a file covers more than one month.
                Averages under this show in red. Default 95.
                A day under this, or blank, shows as NA and is left out of the average. Default 50.
                Inactive people with fewer attended days than this are left out of the reports. Default 6.
                Someone the month's Schedule export has no day for, and with no attendance, is left out of every sheet and every Excel export (the roster keeps them). On by default.
                Deduction scope: brands
                Only these brands are listed in the Deduction sheet. Default Virgin.

                Data from before

                This computer still has what this browser kept before the shared folder: the roster, history, settings, forms and accounts. Copy it into the shared folder once, so everyone has it. Older accounts keep their password; each person signs in once more, and the access opens the next time an admin opens the tool.

                Team copy

                Roles

                • Admin does everything below and manages the accounts. There is always at least one admin.
                • WFM analyst builds the month (imports, roster, settings, workbooks) and the daily emails: in WFM team › Report builder they drop the day's exports, send MC Leaders and the WFM Daily Review, and the four brand emails go to the WFM manager. The rest of the WFM page and the teams are read-only for them, and they do not see the incentive amounts. The month is saved to the shared data as they work.
                • WFM manager sends the four brand emails the analysts made (Virgin Postpaid, Virgin Mobile, FRiENDi Mobile, FRiENDi Pay) from WFM team › Daily emails, adds the interactions export, sends the deduction and absence emails, fixes the accepted objections on adherence and AHT, and sees the analytics, results and every team.
                • Senior manager sees every department, supervisor and agent (the WFM page read-only, without its emails; on the Team page who has a one-to-one arranged and who not yet); sets the supervisors' scorecards, the one-to-one deadline and the month-close due days; changes the incentive rules (with an admin); decides the objections sent to him; sends the one-to-ones-ready, deadline, review and final emails; finalizes each month. After that only he can change the results. He sees every change made by hand.
                • Supervisor (linked to their name in the roster) sees their own team, arranges the one-to-ones (following up last month's actions), reads what each agent wrote and sends the final back (accepted or rejected, with a comment), corrects the team's attendance, answers the agents' objections, approves the agents of the team, and tells the senior manager when the team is done. When you make someone a supervisor here, link them to their name (the operations team is listed) and tick the agents they lead.
                • Quality team drops the Final EVAL (the template with national IDs links every row by itself), corrects the quality KPIs until the month is final, and fixes the accepted objections on quality.
                • Agent (linked to their name) sees only their own results, attendance and forms, fills in their part of the one-to-one and sends it to the supervisor, signs it after the supervisor's final, raises objections, and sees this month so far (in English or Arabic).
                • Waiting for access: anyone who signs up starts here. The admin opens staff accounts; a supervisor opens the accounts of their own agents.

                Getting around

                • Your pages are in the sidebar on the left. On a laptop it narrows to icons (point at one for its name); the button at its foot widens it again, and this browser remembers your choice. On a phone the pages are in the bar at the bottom; with more than five, More holds the rest, and How to use and Settings are in the account menu.
                • Search (Ctrl K) is at the top of the sidebar (on a phone, in the header). The header carries the bell with your notifications: deadlines and what is yours to do (everyone), and the checks (for the people who build the month), the month the page shows and your account. A final month shows a lock and is read-only. On Build the month comes from the exports instead; change it in Settings › Month.
                • Appearance: choose Light, Dark or System in your account menu (your initials, top right) or in Settings. System, the first choice, follows your computer's light or dark setting and changes with it. The choice is kept in this browser.
                • The WFM roles and the senior manager start on the Dashboard: the month's six numbers against the month before, the trend, what needs attention, the senior manager's month close steps and how old each source is. Everyone else starts on their own page; what is theirs to do, with its deadline, is in the bell.
                • WFM team holds the month's build as tabs: Import, Review, Export and Emails, next to Daily, Report builder, Analytics, Agents and Interactions. Review opens on Checks, the same checks as the bell, with what each one means and what happens until you act. Only three things stop a build: an empty roster, files still being read, and no export or attendance file at all.

                Every month

                1. In Genesys Cloud, export the month's Monthly Adherence, Agent Performance Summary, Schedule (activities) and Agent Status Timeline Summary.
                2. Drop all four on Import, with the supervisors' filled attendance templates (TS, MG, CT, QA, DE and WF: Import › Attendance templates makes one file per department for the month, which opens on How to fill: one row per late, absent, leave or day off; CC and SM need none, their days come from the Schedule and the Agent Status Timeline). Each card shows what was found. The bell at the top lists anything the tool fixed, anything you need to decide (for example two files that disagree on a day), and differences between the attendance and Genesys.
                3. On Review, open Issues: link each unknown name to a person as their system name, or add them. When a roster name is clearly one Genesys name, the tool links it by itself (the bell shows it, with Undo). Set people who left to Inactive in People.
                4. People shows a card per agent with their Genesys name, National ID, brand, team and this month's numbers. Point at any agent, anywhere in the tool, for a quick profile; select the card for the full page, where you can edit their details, see their history chart and export it. Switch to Table to edit many people at once.
                5. Check Preview, then press Build Excel.
                6. Performance (optional): export the Agent Performance Summary a second time with every column (Answered, Handle, Avg Handle, Avg Talk, Avg Hold, Avg ACW, Held, Transferred, Outbound) and drop it on Import. Preview then shows each employee's performance with team totals and a sortable table (green at least 15% better than the team, red at least 15% worse), and each person's page compares them with their team. Times are weighted the way Genesys works them out. Exports of past months go to the history, so the person's chart can show answered, handle time, hold, ACW and transfer rate by month. An export with only voice also gives the AHT.
                7. Workforce and exceptions: with the Schedule and Agent Status Timeline in, every scheduled day of the month is judged with the same rules as the Daily WFM & Performance Review (late after 0 min, no sign-on after 180 min, short of shift from 15 min, adherence 95%, AHT ceiling 2:30, high hold 45 s, at least 5 calls; leave days left out) and added up per employee: shifts, worked, no sign-on, late sign-ons and minutes, short of shift, break changes, time signed on, occupancy, conformance and exceptions. Preview shows the totals by team, the priority follow-up list with reasons and a sortable table; each person's page lists their days one by one. Late first call, calls under 10 s, longest calls and dropped calls need the daily Interactions export, so they stay in the daily email.
                8. Build the incentive data workbook too. Both files are filled in, including attendance and tardy minutes.
                9. On WFM team › Emails › Monthly emails, pick Deduction or Incentive, then For review, and where the numbers come from: Shared month (with the supervisors' attendance corrections) or This build (the incentive always comes from the build). Use Copy for Outlook and paste into a new email, or Download .eml and open it in Outlook. The data sent for review is remembered. The WFM manager sends the deduction and absences emails from the same place, from the shared month. The deduction email's attachment (Save attachment) is one workbook with the Attendance Report and the Monthly Deduction; the emails' workbooks carry no National IDs.
                10. Everything you drop on Import is kept (Import › Saved uploads), so signing out loses nothing: the month is back in Build when you sign in again. Pick a month there to load it, move a file to another month, replace or delete it.
                11. On vacation? The WFM manager ticks your name on the WFM team page (Vacation cover) and has your tabs until you are back; when the manager is away, you tick theirs.
                12. After the review deadline, drop any corrected files, open Final, and send. The final email lists what changed since the review.
                13. The daily emails are built into the tool. A WFM analyst drops the day's exports on WFM team › Report builder (on a Sunday, Thursday to Saturday): MC Leaders and the WFM Daily Review are made and sent from there, and Virgin Postpaid, Virgin Mobile, FRiENDi Mobile and FRiENDi Pay appear straight away on the WFM manager's WFM team › Daily emails, where he writes the SLA insight, checks them and sends them (Copy for Outlook or Open in Outlook), then marks each one sent. The emails are made by the same parts as Member Care Report Builder 14, so they look exactly as before. Every day dropped is kept for everyone; building the WFM Daily Review also keeps each agent's day, and a month without monthly exports is shown from the stored days.
                14. Supervisors: drop the Teams Distribution email (.msg) on Import, or paste its table with Review › People › Supervisors…. The tool shows who changes team before anything is saved; names it cannot match are listed so you can fix them in the roster's Supervisor column.
                15. Saving: while you build a month, its results are saved to the shared history by themselves, a few seconds after each change (the line at the top says when). A month already in the history from an older file is kept until you replace it in Review › History, and a month the senior manager has finalized is never overwritten.
                16. For a one-to-one, open a person and use One-to-one form, then Final form after the investigation. Both download as PDF; the one-to-one fits on one page (only a very long discussion runs on to a second).
                17. KPI results: drop the monthly KPI file (DRC-CSAT, Quality, Empowerment, FCR…) on Import. Adherence, AHT, days under target and tardiness come from the exports and the attendance. Review › KPI results shows every agent's ranking, final %, incentive target and earned SR, with PDF cards, Excel and a copy-for-email card. Scorecards are in Settings.
                18. History: drop the past monthly incentive files (MC_all_team_incentive _data) and the Genesys exports of past months (AHT, Agent Performance, Monthly Adherence, Schedule, Agent Status Timeline) on Import or in Review › History. Each file goes to its own month; a month still running is left out. The incentive file's values are kept, and the Genesys exports fill the gaps and add deduction minutes and conformance (only for agents whose schedule covers the whole month, so drop all the schedule files that touch a month together). Each person's page shows their months as a chart, and Review › History shows everyone side by side. The month you send as final is added by itself.

                Late first call, calls under 10 seconds, longest calls, repeat callers and dropped calls need the Interactions export day by day, so they stay in the daily email.

                Rules used

                1. Adherence: a blank day, or one under the NA cut-off, is NA. Avr. is the average of the other days.
                2. Deduction: Sched. is the minutes of On Queue, Break, Meal, Update Break Time and Training. Actual is the time in On Queue, Break, Meal, Training or Meeting during those segments. Diff is Sched. minus Actual, never below 0, and 0 when Actual is 0.
                3. Inactive people with fewer attended days than the limit are left out of every report. They stay in the Roster and are listed in the Overview.
                4. Names: the system name is used when filled, otherwise the name. Spaces and capital letters don't matter.
                5. Attendance: codes like "Off", "AL leave" or "SL leaves" are tidied to OFF, AL and SL. A number in a day cell is tardy minutes; when the day cells and a Tardy column disagree, the day cells are used until you choose. Each fix can be undone from the bell.

                Roles and pages

                • Supervisor › Team: their own agents (the roster's Supervisor column), the team's average of every KPI (their own KPIs as a supervisor), their supervisor scorecard, a one-to-one board, the month's attendance (counted from Genesys for CC and SM, from the supervisor's attendance template for TS, MG, CT, QA, DE and WF; only the supervisor can correct a day), the agents waiting for their approval, and Finish my team, which tells the senior manager in the tool and makes an email draft to him. It stays grey until every agent's one-to-one is done. The one-to-one: arrange it; an agent with an account fills in their part on their own page (what was discussed, the root cause, their comments, actions, the next review date) and sends it; the supervisor reads it, accepts or rejects it with a final comment and sends the final back; only then does the agent sign. For an agent without an account the supervisor fills in the form when they meet. Supervisors do not see the incentive amounts.
                • Senior manager › Supervisors: the one-to-one deadline, which supervisors have finished (a notification and a count on the page button when one does), the supervisors' scorecards and their items (team averages, one-to-ones by the deadline, the quality team's leader items, or items he types), and the month's four emails: one-to-ones ready (to the supervisors), the deadline reminder (to those not finished), the results for review (“Hi All”: the ID, name, final % and earned SR of everyone on the incentive list who earned it, with the same table as an Excel file) and the final result form (his own form: everyone on the incentive list with their final % and earned SR, the month's total and the table the VP, HR Director, Finance Director and CEO sign, as an email and as the same Excel form). The incentive list on the same page says who is on those two, in order, with the names as the tool has them; add or remove people there. The emails carry no logo or name: Outlook adds your signature. Results: every agent; he decides who is eligible against the rules and finalizes the month.
                • WFM: Analytics by team, brand and month; Agents with every measure and the best and worst quarter marked; Daily with the stored days; Report builder (the WFM analysts: the day's exports, MC Leaders, the WFM Daily Review); Daily emails (the WFM manager: the four brand emails to send); Interactions from the interactions export; Emails with the deduction and absences emails (the WFM manager). The senior manager and the analysts read the rest of the page.
                • Team page for the senior manager, the WFM team and the admin: every team; the agents ranked lowest first (adherence, final %, exceptions, absence or tardiness), with a name search and the supervisor under each name.
                • Quality team › Quality: drop the Final EVAL; Call QA fills Quality Observations (CT: the Final Score), critical errors are kept (an attitude error stops the incentive), the Leaders sheet scores the team leads. Any quality KPI can be corrected by hand until the month is final; each change is logged.
                • Agent › My page: only their own results, attendance, daily adherence and forms. They fill in their part of the one-to-one and send it to their supervisor; when the supervisor sends the final back, they read it and sign it on screen, download the signed PDF and email it to themselves and their supervisor.
                • WFM analyst and admin build the month. Incentive: base by brand (Virgin 1000, FRiENDi 500, FRiENDi Pay 500, a person's own base in the roster wins); nobody earns it with a final under 80%, an attitude critical error or fewer than 5 days attended, unless the senior manager decides otherwise.

                Closing a month

                Each step of the close has its day of the next month: the month built from the exports (day 2), the KPI file and the EVAL (day 3), the results on the agents' pages and the ready email (day 5), the objections answered (day 8), the one-to-ones and the review (day 9), the final and the final emails (day 10). Most steps tick themselves when the tool sees them done; the bell reminds the person whose step it is when it is due soon or late, and Mark done there ticks a step done outside the tool. The senior manager changes the days under Supervisors › Due days; the dashboard shows the senior manager's own five steps.

                The bell lists what is each person's to do now: their late or near month-close steps, one-to-ones to hold, objections to answer or fix, agents waiting for approval, forms waiting for a signature, last month's actions to check, a daily review not stored yet, names to link, accounts waiting. Each line opens the place to do it.

                Objections

                An agent who thinks a number is wrong raises an objection on their own page: a day of attendance or adherence (select the day), a KPI, the AHT, the quality result, the incentive, or anything else, with what it should be and why. The window closes on the month's objection day. The supervisor accepts it (attendance is corrected straight away), says why not, or sends it to the senior manager; an agent whose objection was not accepted can ask the senior manager to look, once. An accepted objection that the WFM team, the quality team or the senior manager must correct waits on their page until they mark it fixed. The agent sees every answer. Supervisors › Objections shows each team's dispute rate.

                Coaching that follows up

                A one-to-one starts with what was agreed last month: each action (Done, Partly, Not done) and each KPI then and now (better or worse). The PDF and the agent's copy carry it, and the board shows "Follow-up 2/3". The senior manager can count it in the supervisors' scorecard: add an item from Follow-up of last month's one-to-ones (actions done, or KPIs better).

                This month so far (agents)

                While a month runs, each stored daily review updates every agent's page: the projected final % and incentive if the month stays like this, and the weakest KPI to work on first. The KPIs that come only at the end of the month use last month's values until this month's arrive. Agents can read their page in Arabic (العربية at the top of their page).

                Incentive rules

                The scorecards (KPIs, weights, bands), the incentive bases and who earns the incentive (lowest final %, fewest days attended, months in the job: 6 by default, the incentive starts with the 6th full month, so someone who joined on 1 January earns from June and someone who joined on 18 January from July; it needs the joining date on the roster) are one set of rules. The absence penalty (How it is counted) takes days off the actual days for each Absent day, never for SL or another leave: with 3, one absent day out of 22 leaves 21 − 3 = 18 days, 4 fewer than scheduled. Only the senior manager or an admin changes them (Supervisors › Incentive rules, or Settings › Scorecards); everyone else sees them read-only. Start new rules from a month: that month and the ones after it use the new set, the months before keep theirs, and a final month never changes. Every change is logged.

                Reconcile with the old Excel, and the EVAL with IDs

                While the team still works the old way, drop the old Excel of the month on Results › Reconcile with the old Excel: the final result (ID, Name, Final %, Earned SR), the incentive data workbook and the deduction workbook, up to three at once, or paste the results table from the email. The tool works out which month each file holds (its dates and title before its name), lines every person up by national ID, then by name, and explains each difference by its cause: an own incentive base, days taken off for absences, days counted differently, a different Final % (a KPI with no value), no scorecard for the team, or a month the tool has no result for. The senior manager or an admin fixes the cause: Use these bases (own bases in the incentive rules), Use this rule (the absence penalty), or Take the old value as a logged adjustment; each has Undo. The quality team can download EVAL template with IDs on the Quality page: an EVAL workbook with every agent's national ID, so a filled-in EVAL links every row by its ID.

                Search

                Press Ctrl K (or /) on any page, or click Search, and type in plain words: a name, a measure, a month or a day, a team, a brand, a supervisor or a page. For example Tala AHT, lowest adherence Virgin, adherence below 95%, absent yesterday, below target August, supervisors not finished, one-to-ones not held, my one-to-one, or a how-to question. The answer shows straight away; Tab completes the word being typed, and the buttons under the box add the likely next word. Typos and a few Arabic words are understood.

                The search finds only what your role may see: a supervisor their own team, the quality team the KPI results, an agent their own page. It remembers what you pick, in this browser only, to suggest it first; Clear my searches forgets it.

                The shared folder

                1. Put this HTML in the common folder, with an empty folder next to it, for example MC Data.
                2. The first person opens the HTML in Edge or Chrome, chooses the data folder, and makes the admin account. Everyone else opens the same HTML, chooses the same folder once (the browser remembers it), and makes an account with a username.
                3. The admin gives staff their role in Manage accounts, links supervisors to their name in the roster (only the operations team is listed) and ticks the agents each supervisor leads. Agents choose their supervisor when they sign up; the supervisor approves them.

                The data files are locked: staff accounts open them with the team's key, an agent's account only the agent's own place, both unlocked by the person's password. Opened outside the tool, a file is unreadable. Anyone who can delete files in the common folder can still delete them, so keep the folder's permissions to the people who need it, and keep it in the usual IT backup. Once you have signed in, the tool picks up other people's changes every few seconds.

                After the sign-in, a pill at the top of the page says when the tool is still reading the shared data (with the files read so far), putting the month's saved files back in Build, or reading dropped files; pages still filling say so instead of looking empty.

                Opening the shared data shows what it waits for, with the seconds. If it is slow on one computer, MC Data is often in OneDrive or SharePoint with its files not on that computer yet: right-click it in File Explorer and choose Always keep on this device. A folder choice cancelled, a folder that does not answer, or one whose files cannot be read yet each says so, with what to do.

                Accounts

                Everyone signs in with a username and a password; the sign-up asks no email. The first account becomes the admin. A user who forgets their password asks the admin, who resets it; in the shared folder their access is then opened again by the admin (or, for an agent, by their supervisor).

                Your data

                Export files are read on your computer and never sent anywhere. What is kept: the roster, the months' results (one row per agent), the quality numbers, the forms and signatures, day totals of the daily data and of the interactions export (never the callers' numbers), the month's Genesys exports and attendance sheets as you dropped them (WFM team › Import › Saved uploads), so signing out loses nothing, and every workbook built (Export › Saved workbooks); only the WFM team opens them. A plain copy of a workbook goes to MC Data › MC Reports only when chosen in the build dialog: that copy is not locked.
